instruction: In my file system, add the prefix "YYYY_MM_DD-" to all file names in the ~/downloaded_files/ directory, based on their creation dates, and then move all files not from this year to ~/recycle_bin/.
notes: The actual contents of ~/downloaded_files/ are unknown at planning time, so the problem uses a representative instance of three files (placeholder names and creation dates: one from the current year 2023, two from earlier years); at run time the agent repeats show_file + move_file once per entry returned by show_directory and the counter (count-N objects, next-count chain) is sized to the number of files. Hidden world facts (file-year, candidate prefixed paths, path-in-dir) are static in :init but every action that uses them is gated by knowledge predicates: listed (from show_directory), creation-date-known (from show_file) and current-date-known (from phone.get_current_date_and_time, included because it is in the reference API list even though the current date is given). The rule 'this year -> stays in ~/downloaded_files/, earlier -> ~/recycle_bin/' is encoded as the static table dest-dir-for-year relative to the 2023 current date; both candidate prefixed paths exist per file so that the rule, not the init, selects the destination. A single move_file call performs both the rename (YYYY_MM_DD- prefix) and the relocation. Because STRIPS has no quantified goals, 'all files processed' is tracked with a pending-files counter whose zero element count-0 is a domain constant so supervisor-complete-task can require (pending-files count-0); reaching count-0 entails that every file sits at its correctly prefixed path in the correct directory (the ground-truth start-to-end path mapping). The task asks no question, so complete_task takes no answer.
